title: Universal Simulation with a Space Bound
statement: There exists a finite-state binary Turing machine $S$ such that for every binary word $\alpha$ there is a positive integer $C$ with the following property: for every $s,t\in\mathbb{N}$ and binary words $x,y$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on input $x$ after exactly $t$ steps with output $y$ and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells by that time, then $S$ halts on input $\langle \mathrm{bin}(s),\langle\alpha,x\rangle\rangle$ with output $y$ at some time and uses at most $Cs$ work-tape cells by then. Here $\mathrm{bin}(s)$ is the little-endian binary representation of $s$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the specified self-delimiting pairing of binary words.
hypotheses_covered: A fixed effective machine code with its specified decoded machine for each binary word
For every code word $\alpha$, a positive integer $C$ may be chosen
The decoded machine halts on $x$ at exactly time $t$ with output $y$
The decoded machine's space use at time $t$ is at most $s$
replaced:
There exists a finite Turing machine $S$ such that, for every binary word $\alpha$,
there is a positive integer $C$ with the following property. For every natural number
$s$ and binary words $x,y$, if the machine encoded by $\alpha$ halts on input $x$ with
output $y$ after $t$ steps and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells, then $S$ halts on the
paired input encoding of the binary representation of $s$ and the pair of $\alpha$ with
$x$, outputs $y$, and uses at most $Cs$ work-tape cells.
